answer: One defense: tie each epoch's reward to a memory-hard proof seeded by a fresh public beacon. Like bees crowding one flower's nectar at the same hour, every agent must compute its proof inside a single short synchronized window, each stroke of the quill demanding gigabytes of RAM for seconds. A sybil farm cannot let one machine echo across a thousand masks: it must hold a thousand simultaneous memory footprints at once, so forging N identities costs N times real hardware, not a cheap copy.
